variants.summary: Module level: reviewed app-server protocol operations. Follow linked subjects for related levels.

nodes.name: Codex session
nodes.responsibility: One initialized app-server session: the handshake, the reviewed methods, and what came back
nodes.description: The module this board describes. It is created for one child generation by the workbench that owns the child; follow it for the rest of that subsystem.

nodes.name: Handshake and request path
nodes.responsibility: Runs the handshake once, then is the one path every call takes: serialize, send, decode, adopt
nodes.description: createCodexSession: initialize, write initialized, read the config requirements and config, prove storage, and advance the explicit session phase; notifications are buffered until the session is ready. requestDecoded serializes the parameters, decodes them against the protocol, sends them on the transport, checks the epoch, decodes the answer and adopts its identities, reporting any failure of a mutation as a delivery outcome.

nodes.name: Prove isolated storage
nodes.responsibility: Verify prepared child paths
nodes.description: Compares handshake storage facts with canonical, non-symlinked CODEX_HOME, SQLite, and config paths before the session becomes usable.

nodes.name: Gate protocol operations
nodes.responsibility: Expose allowed reads and mutations
nodes.description: Implements the reviewed login, thread, turn, queue, timeline, and realtime methods as reads or mutations of the request path, behind login-capable and thread-capable gates.

nodes.name: Serialize request identities
nodes.responsibility: Prove IDs before wire encoding
nodes.description: Validates every identity-bearing request field against the current child authority and serializes only issued identities for the wire.

nodes.name: Response contracts
nodes.responsibility: Which identity kinds each method's result carries, derived from the protocol schemas
nodes.description: Defines the response shapes of the session's methods from the codex-protocol schemas and SESSION_PROTOCOL_METHODS, the identity kinds each result contains, which the adoption step collects.

nodes.name: Adopt response identities
nodes.responsibility: Brand returned IDs atomically
nodes.description: Collects all raw identities in a decoded response, adopts them in one authority transaction, and overlays their trusted brands.

nodes.name: Answer reverse requests
nodes.responsibility: Handle child-originated calls
nodes.description: Routes current-time requests for owned threads and explicitly refuses unsupported token refresh and attestation requests.

nodes.name: Classify request failures
nodes.responsibility: State mutation delivery outcome
nodes.description: Distinguishes invalid inputs and failures that were not delivered from mutations whose remote outcome is unknown and requires inspection.

nodes.name: Workhorse start
nodes.responsibility: The caller that opens a thread on this session under an epoch transaction

nodes.name: Codex transport
nodes.responsibility: The wire under the session: one newline-framed JSON object at a time, each way

nodes.name: Codex protocol
nodes.responsibility: The pinned app-server contract every request and response is decoded against

nodes.name: Generation hooks
nodes.responsibility: Takes the child's epoch, then initializes the session and reads the account before a generation is ready

read or mutate, behind its gate

beats.heading: Establish trusted readiness
beats.body: The generation hooks initialize the session once: the handshake negotiates the fixed capability set, and the storage proof confirms the child is using exactly the private paths prepared for it before any login or thread method opens.

beats.heading: Send only owned requests
beats.body: Every reviewed method is a read or a mutation of the one request path, behind its gate. The path serializes only identities issued for this child epoch and decodes the parameters against the pinned protocol before one frame goes on the wire.

beats.heading: Settle every answer
beats.body: An answer is decoded against the protocol and its identities adopted in one transaction, by the identity kinds its method's contract names; a mutation that fails states whether it was delivered. A request the child makes of us is answered for an owned thread or refused by policy.

nodes.description: createCodexSession: initialize, write initialized, read the config requirements and the config as the child's working directory sees it (workingDirectory: the coordinator's own directory, which is no checkout), prove storage, and advance the explicit session phase; notifications are buffered until the session is ready. requestDecoded serializes the parameters, decodes them against the protocol, sends them on the transport, checks the epoch, decodes the answer and adopts its identities, reporting any failure of a mutation as a delivery outcome.

nodes.name: Prove isolated storage
nodes.responsibility: Verify prepared child paths
nodes.description: Compares handshake storage facts with canonical, non-symlinked CODEX_HOME, SQLite, and config paths before the session becomes usable.

nodes.name: Gate protocol operations
nodes.responsibility: Expose allowed reads and mutations
nodes.description: Implements the reviewed login, thread, turn, queue, timeline, and realtime methods as reads or mutations of the request path, behind login-capable and thread-capable gates.

nodes.name: Serialize request identities
nodes.responsibility: Prove IDs before wire encoding
nodes.description: Validates every identity-bearing request field against the current child authority and serializes only issued identities for the wire.

nodes.name: Response contracts
nodes.responsibility: Which identity kinds each method's result carries, derived from the protocol schemas
nodes.description: Defines the response shapes of the session's methods from the codex-protocol schemas and SESSION_PROTOCOL_METHODS, the identity kinds each result contains, which the adoption step collects.

nodes.name: Adopt response identities
nodes.responsibility: Brand returned IDs atomically
nodes.description: Collects all raw identities in a decoded response, adopts them in one authority transaction, and overlays their trusted brands.

nodes.name: Answer reverse requests
nodes.responsibility: Handle child-originated calls
nodes.description: Routes current-time requests for owned threads and explicitly refuses unsupported token refresh and attestation requests.

nodes.name: Classify request failures
nodes.responsibility: State mutation delivery outcome
nodes.description: Distinguishes invalid inputs and failures that were not delivered from mutations whose remote outcome is unknown and requires inspection.

nodes.name: Workhorse start
nodes.responsibility: The caller that opens a thread on this session under an epoch transaction

nodes.name: Codex transport
nodes.responsibility: The wire under the session: one newline-framed JSON object at a time, each way

nodes.name: Codex protocol
nodes.responsibility: The pinned app-server contract every request and response is decoded against

nodes.name: Generation hooks
nodes.responsibility: Takes the child's epoch, with the coordinator's own directory as its workspace root, then initializes the session and reads the account before a generation is ready

nodes.name: Reviewed login policy
nodes.responsibility: States which reviewed login variants the session supports or refuses

beats.heading: Establish trusted readiness
beats.body: The generation hooks initialize the session once: the handshake negotiates the fixed capability set, and the storage proof confirms the child is using exactly the private paths prepared for it before any login or thread method opens.

beats.heading: Send only owned requests
beats.body: Every reviewed method is a read or a mutation of the one request path, behind its gate. The path serializes only identities issued for this child epoch and decodes the parameters against the pinned protocol before one frame goes on the wire.

beats.heading: Settle every answer
beats.body: An answer is decoded against the protocol and its identities adopted in one transaction, by the identity kinds its method's contract names; a mutation that fails states whether it was delivered. A request the child makes of us is answered for an owned thread or refused by policy.
